chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan from Alwan from Al-As said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of Magians who rose up against some Muslims in the land of Islam. He said: 'Yes, and their taking of captives (sabiy).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fighting Magians who rebel in Islamic lands?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on 'People of Deviation,' this hadith clarifies the status of Magians who rebel within Islamic lands, affirming the permissibility of combat and the specific ruling of *sabiy* (taking captives). This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes their status from other *Ahl al-Kitab* in certain contexts, linking their political rebellion to the right of booty and captivity. The narration underscores the practical application of Imam al-Sadiq’s legal reasoning regarding non-Muslims residing under Muslim rule.
